ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows a nuclear reaction equation, with ⁶₃Li plus an unknown “?” on the left, and ⁷₃Li on the right side of the arrow. Then reason: In a nuclear reaction, the mass number and atomic number are conserved. In terms of mass number: 6 + A = 7, so the mass number A of the unknown particle = 1. In terms of atomic number: 3 + Z = 3, so the atomic number Z of the unknown particle = 0. A particle with mass number 1 and atomic number 0 is a neutron.

method.method_draft: Read the image as lithium-6 on the left becoming lithium-7 on the right, while the element remains lithium because the subscript atomic number stays 3 on both sides. From the question text, infer that the missing item is the particle added to lithium-6. Since the isotope changes only by gaining one mass unit while keeping the same proton number, the added particle must be one neutral nucleon rather than a proton or charged particle. A neutral nucleon is a neutron.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中显示核反应为 ⁶₃Li + ? → ⁷₃Li。左边是质量数为 6、原子序数为 3 的锂，右边是质量数为 7、原子序数仍为 3 的锂。推理：反应后元素仍是锂，说明质子数没有改变；质量数从 6 增加到 7，说明增加了一个核子。因为原子序数没有增加，所以增加的不是质子，而是一个不带电的核子，即中子。
